# Commit 1 compatibility fixture

`dungeon_commit1_baseline.json` contains results generated by the **original**
`Scene/Map/dungeon_generator.gd` from commit
`d83caa17534b4355157784e5326e2d701a082fc6`, not by the current generator with variants
disabled. Source blob: `7440f262d7cf598d22f1474b617de796dcf58132`.
The source SHA256, unchanged Commit 1 `world.tscn` SHA256 and exact Godot version
are recorded in the fixture. The regeneration script verifies both source hashes
and requires Godot 4.7.2; passing the current production script is rejected.

The 27 cases cover three seeds (`ALOALO1234`, `BUG_PILLAR_SPAWN_42`, `a`), each at
8/16/32 rooms and floors 1/2/3. Configuration: cell size 40, room bounds 16..25.
Fingerprints include ordered room geometry/types, graph, traps, planned spawns,
exclusion/corridor cells, floor/decor/door tile source/atlas/alternative data, and
the exact final RNG seed/state (64-bit integers stored as decimal strings).
Dictionary entries are sorted before hashing; array order is preserved.

## Regeneration

Work in a temporary copy of the project so importing cannot alter the workspace.
Extract the pinned source with `git show` to a UTF-8 file **outside the repository**
and copy it into that temporary project as `commit1_dungeon_generator.gd`.
Preserve LF line endings and omit a BOM. Verify SHA256:

```text
2d6f587e91bc28cef000b67ff2277d2c6b83e1b318e8516be6b751ebf7feff16
```

After importing the temporary project with Godot 4.7.2, run:

```powershell
& $GodotExecutable --headless --path $TemporaryProject --script res://tests/fixtures/generate_commit1_baseline.gd -- --baseline-script res://commit1_dungeon_generator.gd --output res://tests/fixtures/dungeon_commit1_baseline.json
```

Review the resulting fixture before copying it back. Normal test runs only read
the committed fixture; they never regenerate it and do not require Git or the
old source to be installed. A compatibility failure requires investigation, not
automatic snapshot replacement.

## Test coverage

The existing unit/property scenes remain the entry points. Unit tests cover
metadata reset, real pillar footprints, constrained fallback with zero/one legal
pillar, RNG isolation, and this independent compatibility baseline. Two negative
checks insert an isolated floor pocket and an oversized decoration to confirm
the collision oracle detects unsafe results.

Property tests retain the original 100-seed/five-invariant pass and add 100
distinct seeds distributed over all nine room-count/floor configurations. This
is a balanced matrix of 100 cases, not the full 900-case cross product.

Collision checks read actual TileData polygons and conservatively rasterize their
axis-aligned bounds on the project's square TileSet. They flood-fill both the
whole dungeon and each combat room, then check connected 3x3 body clearance,
entrance approaches and every planned enemy spawn. They do not trust the
generator's cached safe cells or call its connectivity helpers. Conservative
polygon bounds can reject a narrow passage that precise physics would allow;
these checks complement interactive gameplay testing.

Run `res://tests/test_skeleton_king.tscn` as well for active boss spawning, summons,
arena unlocking and portal creation with variants enabled.
